edit.description: the required-argument arm of the count predicate, beside the optional one whose undefined stays a no-op
the width's read through the arm that refuses an absent one
the declared-width cases, whose sentences must not move

summary: a width of `undefined` handed to the partition helper is refused with the wave-width floor sentence rather than filling one unbounded batch
acceptance: `partitionByFileOverlap` called with an absent width refuses it the way a zero or a fraction is refused, and the two surfaces that legitimately fall back on an omitted count keep their byte-identical messages and their no-op
tests: a partition width of undefined is refused rather than filling one unbounded batch
pins: an omitted optional count still falls through to its caller's own default
notes: `assertPositiveCount`'s undefined arm is a strict no-op — right for the two optional fields, wrong for a required argument with no fallback to name. Reachable rather than typed away: a consumer's `chain.ts` is transpiled by `tsx` and never typechecked, so an `order` hook handing the helper `maxParallel: undefined` gets every disjoint entry in one batch. The fix is a second arm, never a check at the call site.
